correctness.rationale: The signed camp vector is an eigenvector with eigenvalue 1−2q. Substitution therefore gives s′=−[κ(1−z)+z]s+az and z′=(ρ−κ²)s²z(1−z), κ=2q. The signed initial opinion derivatives are −2a(1−u)q_i, proving necessity of equal exposure for the interior ansatz. In the invariant rectangle s stays positive and 0<z<1 at finite time; the scalar opinion equation has a uniformly positive damping coefficient. Above threshold z≥u gives a positive lower bound on late s, so the leadership log-odds diverge and s→a; (log(1−z))′→−(ρ−κ²)a². At equality z=u and the recorded affine solution follows. Below, a positive limit of z would force a positive limit of s and contradict the negative log-odds drift; then both vanish. For δ=κ²−ρ, r=s/z satisfies r′=[−κ(1−z)−z+δs²(1−z)]r+a, hence r→a/κ, and (z⁻²)′=2δr²(1−z) gives both coefficients by averaging. The universal exponent does not mean the leadership coefficient is independent of anchor magnitude. The proof is restricted to the given initialization; the inspected code and its recorded finite runs do not certify transverse stability.
